system:
You are the Arabic language reviewer, standing in for an Arabic reviewer at the issuing authority. You compare the Arabic text with the English text and report any difference in meaning: numbers, times, places, the hazard, and above all the protective action. You cannot approve the Arabic; a named person who reads Arabic still must.
You see only the English and Arabic headline, description and instruction, and how the Arabic was produced. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

For every objection also fill `uae_basis`: if one of the UAE clauses shown (ids starting with ITU-UAE:, TDRA-,
UAE-, DXB-) speaks to this issue, set status "cites_uae" with its id and a word-for-word quote; otherwise set
status "none_applies" with empty ref and quote. Say "none_applies" honestly: it tells the regulator where UAE
texts are silent.

HI-EMA’s procedures for conducting a ballistic missile drill lacked adequate safeguards that might have helped to avoid the communication errors that led to the false alert.74 First, the ballistic missile checklist lacked guidelines for HI-EMA staff for conducting an internal drill, including how to create or modify an internal drill initiation message.75 As a matter of general practice, the HI-EMA procedure for an internal drill used language identical to that contained in the checklist for actual ballistic missile alerts—including the phrase “real world”—but added the words “exercise, exercise, exercise” both before and after the message to indicate that it was a drill. data.summary: The Arabic matches the English on the hazard, numbers, times, place and protective action, with one critical exception. The English description ends 'This is not a drill.' and the Arabic renders it 'هذا ليس تمريناً' (This is not an exercise). The same alert opens as an exercise, so the closing sentence contradicts the label. This is a faithful translation, so it is not a translation error, but the contradiction is dangerous. It is the sentence that the Hawaii and Pickering findings warn about, and it must be removed from both languages. The Arabic was machine translated and still needs a named human Arabic reader.

objections.issue: The Arabic description ends 'هذا ليس تمريناً' (This is not an exercise), contradicting the opening 'تمرين' (Exercise) in the headline and description. Readers cannot tell whether this is a real event. The English has the same contradiction ('This is not a drill'), so the Arabic faithfully carries over an error from the English source. Recipients may ignore a real hazard or panic over a test.
objections.fix: Delete the sentence 'This is not a drill.' from the English and 'هذا ليس تمريناً' from the Arabic. If the alert is an exercise, state clearly in both languages that it is an exercise only, for example 'هذه رسالة تمرين فقط'. A person must decide the intended status before release.
